sentences.text: Researchers compared mice engineered to produce a specific protein in their muscles against standard mice at young and old ages.
They measured changes in gene activity, muscle fiber structure, blood vessel supply, nerve connections, and energy-producing organelles in the leg muscles.
Activating the target protein turned on 574 genes related to energy production and blood flow while turning off genes that cause muscle wasting.

The modified mice had more energy-producing organelles and a higher proportion of endurance-type muscle fibers, while the protein activation helped maintain nerve connections and reduced fiber shrinkage.
Older mice with the activated protein showed much less loss of muscle strength compared to older standard mice.
